CORERRTH.name: CORERRTH

fields.name: ERRTH
fields.description: Link correctable error threshold. Non zero threshold value enables the correctable error counter. When the Correctable Error Counter is enabled, an internal ERR_COR message is generated when the counter becomes equal to threshold. If threshold is 15 and count is 14, the next correctable error generates 1 Correctable error message. Same holds true for count and threshold of 0xFFFFFFFF. CORERRCNT.ERRCNT would be saturated, i.e. stops counting at 0xFFFFFFFF accordingly. CXL PM Message Control (CXLPMMCTL) ā€” Offset 7D0h CXL PM Message Control

fields.name: BIST_CORR_MODE
fields.description: When set to 1, PFD is used to correct single device DUE case. If this bit is set to 1, bist_err_report_mode bit should be set to 0.

fields.name: FORCE_METAERROR
fields.description: When final result is UC and correction fsm is UC - meta error follows the meta error indicated by the correction fsm. This bit can be used to force the meta error to 1 always when we have a final result as UC when PFD is enabled.

fields.name: BIST_CE_CORRFSM_NOERR
fields.description: This bit is used to program the final result for the case when PFD gives CE and correction fsm gives NoErorr. Values it can take are: 00 -> UC 01 -> CE 10 -> NoError

fields.name: BIST_ERR_REPORT_MODE
fields.description: This bit is used to indicate if the PFD would work in Error reporting mode. In this mode, we only log the PFD results, but they are not considered to make the final decision in the ecc correction path

fields.name: BIST_EN
fields.description: This bit is used to indicate if the PFD in the ecc corr path is enabled. 13.4.25

fields.name: LEAKY_BKT_2ND_CNTR_LIMIT
fields.description: Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit (2b per DIMM). This register defines secondary leaky bucket counter limit for all 8 logical ranks within channel. The counter logic will generate the secondary LEAK pulse to decrement the ranks correctable error counter by 1 when the corresponding rank leaky bucket rank counter roll over at the predefined counter limit. The counter increment at the primary leak pulse from the LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_LO and LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_HI logic. Bit[31:30]: Rank 7 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[29:28]: Rank 6 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[27:26]: Rank 5 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[25:24]: Rank 4 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[23:22]: Rank 3 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[21:20]: Rank 2 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[19:18]: Rank 1 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit[17:16]: Rank 0 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit The value of the limit is defined as the following: the LEAK pulse is generated after a primary LEAK pulse is received when the rank's corresponding counter in leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr has the value of leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit - 1. When leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit for the rank is 0, it represent the value of 4. After LEAK pulse is generated, the counter is reset to 0. Assuming N = leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit per rank, with N = 4 if leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit = 0, a LEAK pulse is generated every N primary LEAK pulse.

a LEAK pulse is generated every N primary LEAK pulse.

IA32_MC0_STATUS.name: IA32_MC0_STATUS
IA32_MC0_STATUS.description: Machine Check Status Register for Bank 0 (IFU). MSCOD/MCACOD encoding per EDS 19.2.

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank.

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition.

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error.

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected.

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error.

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error.

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status.

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit.

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator.

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code.

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Model Specific Error Code. Refer to Machine Check Encoding section (EDS 19.2).

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code. Refer to Machine Check Encoding section (EDS 19.2).

fields.name: VALID

fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank.

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition.

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error.

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected.

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error.

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error.

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status.

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit.

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator.

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code.

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Model Specific Error Code. Refer to Machine Check Encoding section (EDS 19.2).

fields.name: TP
fields.description: When set, this bit indicates that the function has issued Non-Posted REquests that have not been completed. For Root or Switch port, it applies to Non-Posted Requests the port has issued on its own behalf (Port's Request ID). A function reports this bit cleared only when all outstanding Non-Posted Requests have completed. Functions that do not issue Non-Posted requests on their own behalf hardwire this bit to 0b.

fields.name: URD

fields.name: FED

For devices supporting Advanced Error Handling, errors are logged in this register regardless of the settings of the correctable error mask register.

fields.name: NFED

For devices supporting Advanced Error Handling, errors are logged in this register regardless of the settings of the correctable error mask register.

fields.name: CED

fields.name: AEMN
fields.description: Advanced Error Interrupt Message Number (AEMN): This register indicates which MSI/MSI-X vector is used for the interrupt message generated in association with any of the status bits of this Capability. For MSI, the value in this register indicates the offset between the base Message Data and the interrupt message that is generated. Hardware is required to update this field so that it is correct if the number of MSI Messages assigned to the Function changes when software writes to the Multiple Message Enable field in the MSI Message Control register. For MSI-X, the value in this register indicates which MSI-X Table entry is used to generate the interrupt message. The entry must be one of the first 32 entries even if the Function implements more than 32 entries. For a given MSI-X implementation, the entry must remain constant. If both MSI and MSI-X are implemented, they are permitted to use different vectors, though software is permitted to enable only one mechanism at a time. If MSI-X is enabled, the value in this register must indicate the vector for MSI-X. If MSI is enabled or neither is enabled, the value in this register must indicate the vector for MSI. If software enables both MSI and MSI-X at the same time, the value in this register is undefined.

fields.name: FEMR

fields.name: NFEMR
fields.description: Non-Fatal Error Messages Received (NFEMR) Set when one or more Non-Fatal Uncorrectable error Messages have been received.

fields.name: FUF
fields.description: First Uncorrectable Fatal (FUF) Set when the first Uncorrectable error Message or PCI_error Message received is for a Fatal error.

fields.name: MEFR
fields.description: Multiple ERR_FATAL/NONFATAL Received (MEFR) Set when either a Fatal or a Non-fatal error is received and ERR_FATAL/NONFATAL Received is already Set.

fields.name: EFR
fields.description: ERR_FATAL/NONFATAL Received (EFR) Set when a Fatal or a Non-fatal error Message is received and this bit is not already Set.

fields.name: MCER
fields.description: Multiple ERR_COR Received (MCER) Set when a Correctable error Message is received and ERR_COR Received is already Set.

fields.name: CER
fields.description: ERR_COR Received (CER) Set when a Correctable error Message is received and this bit is not already Set.

fields.name: MRRS
fields.description: This field sets the maximum Read Requests size for the function as a requester. The Function must not generate read requests with size exceeding the set value. 000b: 128 bytes maximum Read Request size 001b: 256 bytes maximum Read Request size 010b: 512 bytes maximum Read Request size 011b: 1024 bytes maximum Read Request size continued... Registers Bit Default and Field Name (ID): Description Range Access 100b: 2048 bytes maximum Read Request size 101b: 4096 bytes maximum Read Request size Others: Reserved Functions that do not generate Read Requests larger than 128B and functions that do not generate Read Requests on their own behalf are permitted to implement this field as Read Only (RO) with a value of 000b.

fields.name: ENOSNP
fields.description: If this bit this is set, the function is permitted to set the No Snoop bit in the Requester attributes of transactions it initiates that do not require hardware enforced cache coherency. This bit is permitted to be hardwired to 0b if a function would never set the No Snoop attribute in transactions it initiates.

fields.name: AUXPME
fields.description: Not Supported

fields.name: PFE
fields.description: When set, this bit enables a function to user unclaimed functions as phantom functions to extend the number of outstanding transaction identifiers. Functions that do not implement this capability hardware this bit to 0b.

fields.name: ETFE
fields.description: When set, this bit enables a function to use an 8-bit tag field as a Requester. Functions that do not implement this capability hardwire this bit to 0b.

fields.name: MPS
fields.description: This field sets maximum TLP payload size for the function. As a receiver, the function must handle TLPs as larger as the set value. As a Transmitter, the function must not generate TLPs exceeding the set value. 000b: 128 bytes maximum payload size 001b: 256 bytes maximum payload size 010b: 512 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) 011b: 1024 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) 100b: 2048 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) 101b: 4096 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) Others: Reserved

fields.name: ENRO
fields.description: When set, the function is permitted to set the relaxed ordering bit in the attribute field of transactions it initiates that do not require strong write ordering. A function is permitted to hardwire this bit to 0b if it never sets the Relaxed ordering attribute in transactions it initiates as a requester.

fields.name: URRE
fields.description: This bit controls the enabling of ERR_CORR, ERR_NONFATAL or ERR_FATAL messages on PCIe* for reporting 'Unsupported Request' errors.

fields.name: FERE
fields.description: When this bit is set, generation of the ERR_FATAL message is enabled.

fields.name: NFERE
fields.description: When this bit is set, generation of the ERR_NONFATAL message is enabled.

fields.name: CERE
fields.description: When this bit is set, generation of the ERR_CORR message is enabled.

ERR_CNTR_CTL.eds_description: Saturating error counters (6b) in B2CMI, this register tracks the number of transactions which had a memory controller error. A transaction in this context is a read transaction from the Bridge (NOT commands to iMC). So even if multiple retries are sent to the memory controller, the retried commands to the iMC are not counted individually.This control register allows indirect access to these B2CMI TXn error counters (reading or clearing).When performing a mirror scrub read, it can either return with (uncorrectable) error or no/corrected error and hence will be counted as either a MIRRSCRUBRD_NOERR or MIRRSCRUBRD_ERR type.Whatever led to the mirror scrub will also be counted as either LINK_TRANSIENT, ECC_CORRECTED or UNCORRECTABLE type.Because mirroring implementation goes to the mirrored channel and gets the data from that channel (to minimize the probability for miscorrections) even on an ECC correctable error, the ECC_CORRECTED type needs to be interpreted as an ECC correctable type (as long as channel does not failed over).A 13.1.30 R Intel® Xeon® 6900/6700/6500-Series Processors with P-Cores-Integrated Memory Controller (IMC) Registers Intel® Xeon® 6900/6700/6500-Series Processors with P-Cores Registers Specification June 2025 5650 Intel Confidential Doc. ERROR COUNTER CONTROL (ERR_CNTR_CTL) - Offset 2B0h
Saturating error counters (6b) in B2CMI, this register tracks the number of
transactions which had a memory controller error. A transaction in this context is a
read transaction from the Bridge (NOT commands to iMC). So even if multiple retries
are sent to the memory controller, the retried commands to the iMC are not counted
individually.This control register allows indirect access to these B2CMI TXn error
counters (reading or clearing).When performing a mirror scrub read, it can either
return with (uncorrectable) error or no/corrected error and hence will be counted as
either a MIRRSCRUBRD_NOERR or MIRRSCRUBRD_ERR type.Whatever led to the
mirror scrub will also be counted as either LINK_TRANSIENT, ECC_CORRECTED or
UNCORRECTABLE type.Because mirroring implementation goes to the mirrored
channel and gets the data from that channel (to minimize the probability for
miscorrections) even on an ECC correctable error, the ECC_CORRECTED type needs to
be interpreted as an ECC correctable type (as long as channel does not failed over).A

fields.name: LEAKY_BKT_CFG_HI
fields.description: This is the higher order bit select mask of the two hot encoding threshold. The value of this field specify the bit position of the mask: 00h: reserved 01h: LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_LO bit 1, i.e. bit 12 of the full 53b counter ... 1Fh: LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_LO bit 31, i.e. bit 42 of the full 53b counter 20h: LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_HI bit 0, i.e. bit 43 of the full 53b counter ... 29h: LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_HI bit 9, i.e. bit 52 of the full 53b counter 2Ah - 3F: reserved continued... (IMC) Registers Bit Default and Field Name (ID): Description Range Access When both counter bits selected by the LEAKY_BKT_CFG_HI and LEAKY_BKT_CFG_LO are set, the 53b leaky bucket counter will be reset and the logic will generate a LEAK pulse to decrement the correctable error counter by 1. MRC BIOS must program this register to a non-zero value before switching to NORMAL mode.

fields.name: LEAKY_BKT_CFG_LO

SPARING_PATROL_STATUS.name: SPARING_PATROL_STATUS

fields.name: PATROL_COMPLETE
fields.description: All memory has been scrubbed. Hardware sets this bit each time the patrol engine steps through all memory locations. If software wants to monitor 0 to 1 transition after the bit has been set, the software will need to clear the bit by writing a one to clear this bit in order to distinguish the next patrol scrub completion. Clearing the bit will not affect the patrol scrub operation. Note, when mirroring is enabled, this bit will be set to 1 after either primary or secondary address scrubbing is done. If software clears this bit to observe 0 to 1 transition, the transition will happen twice to get full address scrubbed.

fields.name: COPY_COMPLETE
fields.description: Sparing copy operation complete. Set by hardware once operation is complete. This bit is cleared by hardware when a new operation is enabled.

fields.name: COPY_IN_PROGRESS
fields.description: This bit indicates that the sparing copy operation is in progress. This bit is set by hardware once the sparing copy has started. It is cleared by hardware once the copy operation is complete or fails.

PME Pending (PMEPEND):
This field indicates that another PME is pending when the PME Status bit is set.
When the PME Status bit is cleared by software, the pending PME is delivered by
hardware by setting the PME Status bit again and updating the Requestor ID
appropriately. The PME pending bit is cleared by hardware if no more PMEs are
pending.
NOTE: The root port can handle two outstanding PM_PME messages in its
internal queues of the Power Management controller per port. If the downstream
device issues more than 2 PM_PME messages successively, it will be dropped.

satellite_ieh:PCISTS.name: PCISTS

fields.name: DPE
fields.description: This bit is set when a poisoned TLP is received. This is set even when the parity erRO/Vr response enable bit is not set.

fields.name: SSE
fields.description: This bit is set when ERR_FATAL or ERR_NONFATAL msg are set to the RO/Vot complex event collector and the SERR enable bit in the PCICMD Register is set.

fields.name: RMA
fields.description: This bit is set when the requester receives a completion status with an UR. On type 1 configuration header functions, the bit is set when a UR is received on the primary side. Registers

fields.name: RTA
fields.description: This bit is set when the requester receives a CA completion status. On type 1 configuration header functions, the bit is set when a Completer Abort is received on the primary side.

fields.name: STA
fields.description: This bit is set when the switch generates a completion packet with Completer Abort (CA) status is generated by its primary side.

fields.name: DEVSEL
fields.description: DEVSEL Timing This field was originally described in the PCI Local Bus Specification. Its functionality does not apply to PCIe* and the field must be hardwired to 00b.

fields.name: MDPD
fields.description: This bit is set by a requester (primary side of type1 configuration header functoions) if the parity erRO/Vr response enable bit (PERE in the command register is set and either of the following two conditions occur: 1. Requester receives a completion marked poisoned 2. requester poisons a write request. If the parity erRO/Vr bit is 0b, this bit is never set.

fields.name: FB2BTE
fields.description: Fast Back-to-Back Transactions Capable This bit was originally described in the PCI Local Bus Specification. Its functionality does not apply to PCIe* and the bit must be hardwired to 0b.

fields.name: SIXTYSIXMHZEN
fields.description: 66 MHz Capable This bit was originally described in the PCI Local Bus Specification. Its functionality does not apply to PCIe* and the bit must be hardwired to 0b.

fields.name: CAPE
fields.description: This bit indicates the presence of an Extended capabilities list items. Offset 34H indicates the offset for the first entry in the linked list of capabilities. All PCIe* Functions are required to have a PCIe* Capability Structure. So this bit must be hardwired to 1b.

fields.name: INTS
fields.description: When set, this bit indicates that an INTx emulation interrupt is pending internally in this function. For Type 1 configuration header functions, forwarded INTx messages are not reflected in this bit. unless the INTx messages is being generated fRO/Vm the Type 1 configuration header function.

fields.name: IR
fields.description: Immediate Readiness (IR): This optional bit, when Set indicates the Function is guaranteed to be ready to successfully complete valid configuration accesses at any time following any reset that the host is capable of issuing configuration requests to this function.

fields.name: MRRS
fields.description: This field sets the maximum Read Requests size for the function as a requester. fields.name: ENOSNP
fields.description: If this bit this is set, the function is permitted to set the No Snoop bit in the Requester attributes of transactions it initiates that do not require hardware enforced cache coherency. This bit is permitted to be hardwired to 0b if a function would never set the No Snoop attribute in transactions it initiates.

fields.name: AUXPME
fields.description: Not Supported

fields.name: PFE
fields.description: When set, this bit enables a function to user unclaimed functions as phantom functions to extend the number of outstanding transaction identifiers. Functions that do not implement this capability hardware this bit to 0b.

fields.name: ETFE
fields.description: When set, this bit enables a function to use an 8-bit tag field as a Requester. Functions that do not implement this capability hardwire this bit to 0b.

fields.name: MPS
fields.description: This field sets maximum TLP payload size for the function. As a receiver, the function must handle TLPs as larger as the set value. As a Transmitter, the function must not generate TLPs exceeding the set value. 000b: 128 bytes maximum payload size 001b: 256 bytes maximum payload size 010b: 512 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) 011b: 1024 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) 100b: 2048 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) 101b: 4096 bytes maximum payload size (Unsupported) Others:

fields.name: ENRO
fields.description: When set, the function is permitted to set the relaxed ordering bit in the attribute field of transactions it initiates that do not require strong write ordering. A function is permitted to hardwire this bit to 0b if it never sets the Relaxed ordering attribute in transactions it initiates as a requester.

fields.name: URRE
fields.description: This bit controls the enabling of ERR_CORR, ERR_NONFATAL or ERR_FATAL messages on PCIe* for reporting 'Unsupported Request' errors.

fields.name: FERE
fields.description: When this bit is set, generation of the ERR_FATAL message is enabled.

fields.name: NFERE
fields.description: When this bit is set, generation of the ERR_NONFATAL message is enabled.

fields.name: CERE
fields.description: When this bit is set, generation of the ERR_CORR message is enabled.

fields.description: This controls the delay between irdy signal (from mmsg_arb to packet merging logic) to trdy signal ( from packet merging logic to mmsg_arb ). This delay is needed to ensure that under regular case, where credits are free flowing, the packets don't have to merge.

fields.description: This is chicken bit for deadlock fix. It will be RW bit. When 0, the packet merging is not done ( survivability mode ). When 1, the packet merging is done. i.e. deadlock fix is in effect.

fields.name: IOMCA_EN
fields.description: This bit is programmed by BIOS if IOMCA is enabled. Moved from Ubox to IEH since IEH sends FULLBANK_MCA_MSG for IOMCA logging.

satellite_ieh:ERRPINDATA.name: ERRPINDATA

fields.name: ERR2_PINDATA
fields.description: (applies when ERRPINCNTL[5:4]=01; otherwise reserved). This bit acts as the general purpose output for the ERR[2] pin. ERR[2] pin value will follow the value programmed in ERR[2] Pin Data register. This bit applies only when ERRPINCTRL[5:4]=01; otherwise it is reserved. • 0 - Assert ERR[2] pin. • 1 - Dessert ERR[2] pin

fields.name: ERR1_PINDATA
fields.description: (applies when ERRPINCNTL[3:2]=01; otherwise reserved). This bit acts as the general purpose output for the ERR[1] pin. ERR[1] pin value will follow the value programmed in ERR[1] Pin Data register. This bit applies only when ERRPINCTRL[3:2]=01; otherwise it is reserved. with P-Cores • 0 - Assert ERR[1] pin. • 1 - Dessert ERR[1] pin

fields.name: ERR0_PINDATA
fields.description: (applies when ERRPINCNTL[1:0]=01; otherwise reserved). This bit acts as the general purpose output for the ERR[0] pin. ERR[0] pin value will follow the value programmed in ERR[0] Pin Data register. This bit applies only when ERRPINCTRL[1:0]=01; otherwise it is reserved. • 0 - Assert ERR[0] pin. • 1 - Dessert ERR[0] pin

IA32_MC0_CTL2.name: IA32_MC0_CTL2

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: MCE_CTL
fields.description: Controls MCE Remapping: 0: MCE, 1: MSMI

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CMCI_CTL
fields.description: Controls CMCI Remapping: 0: CMCI, 1: CSMI

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this bit is writeable but will always return 0 for that bank. This bit also indicates CMCI is supported or not supported in the corresponding bank.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

eds_refs.parent_section_title: Model Specific Registers (MSRs)

pcie_root_port:ERRUNCMSK.eds_description: This register controls the reporting of individual uncorrectable errors by device to the host bridge via a PCIe* error message. This register also controls the logging of the header. Refer to the PCIe* specifications for details of how the mask bits function. A masked error (respective bit set in the mask register) is not reported to the host bridge by the switch, nor is the header logged (status bits unaffected by the mask bit). There is a mask bit per bit of the Uncorrectable Error Status Register. The attr. of AER Error Mask bits in VRSP will be changed to be compliant with PCIe Spec.
